AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: Percutaneous endoscopic contralateral interlaminar lumbar foraminotomy (PECILF) for lumbar degenerative spinal stenosis is an established procedure. Better preservation of contralateral facet joint compared to that of the approach side has been demonstrated with uniportal bilateral decompression. The aim of this retrospective case series was to analyze the early clinical and radiological outcomes of standalone contralateral foraminotomy and lateral recess decompression using PECILF.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Twenty-six consecutive patients with unilateral lower limb radiculopathy underwent contralateral foraminotomy and lateral recess decompression using PECILF. Their clinical outcomes were evaluated with Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) leg pain score, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) and MacNab's criteria. Completeness of decompression was documented with a postoperative MRI.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Mean age for the study group was 62.9±9.2 years and the male:female ratio was 4:9. Total 30 levels were decompressed with 18 patients(60%) undergoing decompression at L4-L5, 9 at L5-S1(30%), two at L3-L4(6.7%) and one at L2-L3( 3.3%). Mean estimated blood loss was 27mL±15mL per-level. Mean operative duration was 48±12 minutes/level. VASleg score improved from 7.7±1 to 1.8±0.8(p <0.0001). ODI improved from 64.4±5.8 to 21±4.5(p <0.0001). Mean follow-up of the study was 13.7±2.7 months. According to MacNab's criteria, 10(38.5%) patients had good results, 14(53.8%) patients had excellent results and 2 patients(7.7%) had fair results. One patient required revision surgery.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Facet preserving contralateral foraminotomy and lateral recess decompression with PECILF is effective for treatment of lateral recess and foraminal stenosis. Thorough decompression with acceptable early clinical outcomes and minimal perioperative morbidity can be obtained with the contralateral endoscopic approach.
